title: Why NodeVideo Does Not Let AI Edit Video Directly
description:
An AI-narrated prototype of my two-minute answer to an applied-agents backend interviewer.

NodeVideo separates language-model planning from durable workflow state and deterministic media execution. The model proposes and explains typed edits. Convex owns leases, checkpoints, versions, and approvals. Fixed tools own frame math and encoding.

The proof boundary matters: 22 targeted reliability tests pass. An integrated edit matched source identity on 5 of 5 phrases, but only 1 of 5 assigned cut boundaries met the timing gate, so the strict editorial verdict failed.

Canonical CreatorBench statement: On creatorbench-v1.4, covering 1392 private held-out workflow instances from 50 creator-disjoint sources across 6 workflows, NodeVideo routed 49.4% to human review and safely abstained in 50.6%. No automatic or assisted usability claim is made because only 0/1392 results have human review. Editing-quality silent-failure incidence remains unverified.

CreatorBench limitations:
No result is classified usable until a rendered artifact is blindly reviewed by a human.
This baseline measures request ingestion, rights validation, route eligibility, and honest non-success states—not editing quality.
Editing-quality silent-failure incidence is unverified: 0/1392 private held-out results have human review.

This video is a manual NodeVideo × NodeSlide Expression Loop dogfood artifact, not a claim that the complete coaching workflow is already implemented. Narration uses a generic synthetic system voice, not a clone of my voice. No AI-generated music or photorealistic synthetic person is used.
